title: Externally anchored permit-ledger integrity

pre_execution_hardening.detail: Checkpoint predecessor validation was corrected before the frozen P4 endpoint execution so a legitimate higher-generation checkpoint could authenticate its predecessor without requiring the predecessor to equal the changed current database state. No frozen endpoint was changed and this was not a repair of a failed scientific result.

supported_claim: On the tested same-host prototype, a platform-held HMAC-authenticated checkpoint stored outside the SQLite permit database, together with a trusted minimum checkpoint generation and canonical ledger digest, detected the preregistered consumed-status resurrection, row deletion, payload rewrite, binding-digest rewrite, epoch lowering, coherent database rollback, stale database/checkpoint substitution, forged or mutated checkpoint, scope and predecessor tampering, and repeated-restart tampered bundles. Canonical row ordering was invariant and the clean higher-generation checkpoint remained live.
not_proven: Integrity when an attacker compromises both the SQLite database and the separate integrity key/checkpoint authority or trusted-minimum state
next_falsification_target: EXP-I Pilot 5: use-time checkpoint binding and consume-checkpoint reconciliation, including stale positive verification reuse and crash/ambiguity between durable permit consumption and checkpoint advancement.
